newsitem.title: UK: M&S leads retailers lower on rate, tax fears.
newsitem.headline: M&S leads retailers lower on rate, tax fears.

text.p: UK Retail stocks dropped on Monday as the prospect of tighter credit prompted a round of profit-taking in a sector that has been one of the main motors of the UK equity market this year, traders said.

Marks & Spencer Plc led the decline, down 7-1/2p at 501 by 1404 GMT. Others also fell, with Next Plc down 11-1/2p at 556-1/2, Dixons Group Plc off 2-1/2p at 558 and Great Universal Stores Plc 12p lower at 625-1/2.
Strategists at BZW said in a research note today that retail shares were showing signs of running out of steam and it could be time to cash in on the sector's gains.

"A fair amount has already been discounted in current prices" of retail stocks, said BZW strategist Steve Wright. "It is the case that the peak in the sector tends to come earlier than the peak in consumer spending."

Wright said the threat of a rise in interest rates and the possibility that whoever wins the UK general election, to be held by next May, will have to tighten fiscal policy, could act as a drag on the sector's performance from here.
